location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge (last sentences: legacy fields rebuilt from the final cells; `pass` = no findings and no `parallel-unconfirmed` cell; `skipped_browser` = every engine's cell has `launch_error`)
issue: If you apply the formula as written, a version where no engine was tested still reports `pass: true`. Three cases hit this: (a) every worker crashes or cannot be spawned; (b) the sequential-fallback snapshot fails, so every cell is `sequential-reset`; (c) every engine has a `launch_error`. In each case `browsers` is [] and findings are empty, so `pass` = true. In (a) and (b), `skipped_browser` is also false, because crash and sequential-reset cells have `launch_error` null. Today's code is different: `_run_one_version_inner` returns `pass: false` and `skipped_browser: true` when `res["browsers"]` is empty. So this is also a regression for case (c). The bullet also does not say whether the rebuild covers the sequential-fallback and single-engine modes. It sits in the parallel-mode merge note, yet sequential-reset cells only exist in the sequential fallback. Today's code there gives `pass: true` when chromium passes and firefox is sequential-reset, and leaves no legacy note.
implementation_impact: The implementer either follows the formula and ships a direct-run output that says pass for an untested version, against the honesty law. Or they keep today's early return and contradict the spec. They also have to guess whether the rebuild runs in every mode. The direct-run exit code stays correct (1), but `versions[ver].pass` and top-level `pass` become wrong. These are the fields the quickstart TDD loop shows to the operator.
suggestion: Define the rule for all modes: `pass` = at least one engine in `browsers` AND no findings AND no `parallel-unconfirmed`, `sequential-reset` or `crash` cell. Keep `skipped_browser` = true when `browsers` is empty (today's semantics), or state the new meaning explicitly. Add a unit check for case (a) and for the snapshot-failure case of the sequential fallback.

location: Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell (failure = timeout, exception, non-zero exit or missing sentinel) and Phases/Confirmation passes (END outcome specified only for `rerun-seq:<engine>`); Tasks > docs (run-phases.md remediation reads the `snapshot-db`/`reset-*`/`rerun-seq:` END lines)
issue: The spec does not give the END outcome, or the `boot_phases` outcome, of a `snapshot-db`, `reset-db`, `reset-files` or `reset-opcache` phase that fails without raising. A non-zero exit or a missing `PSM_*_OK` sentinel comes back as a normal `CompletedProcess`. `fl.phase.__exit__` then writes `END ok` and records outcome `ok` unless the code sets `ph.status`, and the spec never asks for that. The same gap applies to the reset routine's `wait-http` when there is no response. Today's first-boot `wait-http` also ends `ok` whether or not it got a response. Only the wrapping `rerun-seq:<engine>` gets `<sub-phase>-failed`. The BO-login fallback and the sequential fallback have no wrapping phase at all.
implementation_impact: Operators are told to diagnose `parallel-unconfirmed` and `sequential-reset` from these END lines. Those lines could read `ok` while the cell says the same sub-phase failed. The same holds for the timing report built from `boot_phases`. Each implementer picks a token (e.g. `failed`, `error(...)`, `<sub-phase>-failed`), and tests on the 'Unconfirmable' and 'Sequential reset fails' rows cannot assert one.
suggestion: State that every failing sub-phase sets its own `ph.status` to a fixed token, e.g. `failed` (keep `timeout` for timeouts), so its END line and `boot_phases[<name>].outcome` show the failure. The reset routine's `wait-http` should do the same when there is no response. Add this to the I/O rows 'Unconfirmable' and 'Sequential reset fails'.

location: Design Notes > Confirmation passes ('After the first failure of the snapshot or of any reset-routine sub-phase … that engine and every later engine needing a pass get `parallel-unconfirmed` … inside `rerun-seq:<engine>`, sets that phase's END outcome … a later engine skipped for it opens no phase'); I/O matrix
issue: The text is written for a failure that happens inside an engine's pass, and leaves the parallel-mode snapshot failure undefined. That failure happens before any worker runs. (1) It does not say outright that the lockstep pass still runs after `snapshot-db` fails. Slots says the sequential fallback then drives no engine at all, so the opposite reading is plausible. (2) Once workers finish, it is unclear whether the first engine needing a pass is 'that engine'. If it is, does it open `rerun-seq:<engine>` with END `snapshot-db-failed`? Or is it 'skipped' and opens no phase? That decides whether its `phase_durations` holds a `rerun-seq:` entry. (3) It is unclear when the `errors` entry is printed to stderr: at snapshot time, when the first engine needs a pass, or not at all when no engine needs one. No I/O row covers a parallel-mode snapshot failure.
implementation_impact: Two reasonable implementations give different `phase_durations`, progress-log lines and stderr for the same run, and 'test every I/O row' never checks either. An implementer who reads Slots by analogy might stop the parallel version after a snapshot failure and lose evidence for engines that needed no confirmation.
suggestion: Add one sentence and one I/O row. Example: 'In parallel mode a `snapshot-db` failure does not stop the lockstep pass; its `errors` entry is printed once at snapshot time; no engine opens `rerun-seq:`; every engine needing a pass gets `parallel-unconfirmed` with `snapshot-db: <reason>` in cell `errors`; engines needing none keep their parallel result.'

location: Acceptance Criteria 1 (unit: 'the real stub-worker spawn test … max(started_at) < min(finished_at) (worker-stamped)'); Tasks > tests ('the worker spawn path once with a real stub worker subprocess'; 'workers spawned through the seam')
issue: A subprocess does not inherit the test's monkeypatches, so the spec has to say how a 'real stub worker' gets a stubbed drive. It names no mechanism (env var, injectable command list, stub-module path) and no seam. If the stub is a separate script launched through a command seam, the real `--engine-worker` code is never run as a subprocess. That code covers argv dispatch before `run_main_with_progress`, `progress_attach`, `job_register`, the `started_at`/`finished_at` stamping inside `browser:<engine>`, and the atomic result write. AC1's 'worker-stamped' overlap would then prove a property of the stub. If the stub is the real worker with an injected drive, the spec does not say how the injection reaches the child process.
implementation_impact: The implementer invents a test-only injection path in production code, or tests a stand-in script. Either way the AC1 unit leg can pass while the real worker never stamps, writes its result, or registers correctly. Those defects would surface only in the live suite.
suggestion: Name the seam and the injection. For example: `WORKER_CMD` (list prefix, default `[sys.executable, __file__]`), plus a worker-only env var such as `PSM_E2E_WORKER_STUB=<path to a module exposing drive_engine>`, which the `--engine-worker` path loads in place of Playwright. State that AC1's unit leg runs the real `ps-e2e-run.py --engine-worker` with that stub, so stamping, result writing and registration are exercised.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (forced cost 1 for `parallel-unconfirmed` history); Design Notes > Logging (the `--sequential-browsers` stderr text drops 'admisi interim cost 1')
issue: A version can now run sequentially for two reasons: free slots were short, or its history holds `parallel-unconfirmed`. Neither ps-run-layer nor the child is told to record which one. The child sees only `--sequential-browsers`. Its notice no longer says why, and the CAP-3 wording that told it apart from slot shortage is dropped. The spec does not ask ps-run-layer to log the forced admission in its stderr or in the version's progress log.
implementation_impact: An operator sees a version drive its browsers one after another while slots were free, with nothing in stderr or the progress log to explain it. Live tests (b) and (c) must fail 'naming the counted slots' when admission fell back. When the cause is history, the slot count is the wrong explanation, and the test cannot tell the two causes apart.
suggestion: Have ps-run-layer log the admission decision per version: cost, mode and reason (`slots` or `parallel-unconfirmed history: <ver>:<browser>`). Write it to stderr and as the detail of the `END wait-slots` line, and let the live test report that reason.
